transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Well, doctor, I'm here because I go to great lengths to avoid getting on an airplane, even when it means missing important family events. My children are starting to get really frustrated with me, and I've realized my world is shrinking because of this fear.
Can you tell me more about what specifically happens or what you experience when you think about getting on an airplane that makes you want to avoid it?

Just the mention of it makes my heart start pounding and my hands go clammy, and I picture the plane dropping out of the sky so vividly that I have to change the subject or walk away. The thought of being sealed in a metal tube at 30,000 feet with no way out just terrifies me, and it feels like I'd be signing my own death warrant if I got on a plane again at my age.

Is your fear primarily focused on the physical aspects of the airplane, such as crashing or the feeling of being trapped, or is it more about what others might think of you if you were to panic or behave anxiously on the plane?

My fear is entirely about the physical aspects of the flight, not at all about what other people might think of me. It's the terrifying feeling of being sealed in a metal tube with no way out, and that vivid image of the plane dropping out of the sky. At my age, getting on a plane just feels like signing my own death warrant.
Have you experienced similar intense fears or avoidance behaviors towards other situations or objects, or is your fear specifically and exclusively related to flying?

No, doctor, this fear is completely and strictly limited to flying. I don't have any other fears or avoidance behaviors like this with other situations or objects in my life. It is only airplanes and air travel that terrify me.
